title: Lemma 2.2: linearity of reduced group action unproven for general strata

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** Lemma 2.2 and its proof (§2.2).

The whole structure theorem rests on $\bar G$ acting LINEARLY (cyclic part diagonally/monomially) on the coefficient space $\mathbb A^n=\operatorname{Spec}k[a_1,\dots,a_n]$. This is verified ONLY for the hyperelliptic stratum ($\delta=2$). For general signature the proof merely asserts '$\bar G$ acts by the same kind of finite linear formulas.'

This is unjustified and **not true in general**: for $\bar G$ dihedral of larger order or $\bar G\in\{A_4,S_4,A_5\}$, $\bar G$ contains Möbius maps $x\mapsto(ax+b)/(cx+d)$ beyond scalings/inversion. These act on the coefficient vector of the normalized model NONLINEARLY: after substitution one must re-normalize (re-clear denominators / rescale to fixed leading and constant coefficients), introducing rational dependence. Only the diagonal scalings $x\mapsto\zeta x$ act monomially.

**Consequence:** the 'toric ⇒ binomial' conclusion (Thm 3.4(d)) depends entirely on the action being diagonal on monomials; for non-diagonal $\bar G$ this fails, and the linear-quotient framing that underlies the entire paper is unestablished outside the hyperelliptic / pure-cyclic case.

**Fix:** either (i) restrict the toric/binomial theorem to strata with $\bar G=\bar G^\circ$ diagonal and treat other $\bar G$ by general finite-linear-group invariant theory — after first PROVING the action is linear post-normalization; or (ii) give explicit transformation formulas for each generator of $\bar G$ on $(a_1,\dots,a_n)$ along the classical $\bar G$-list and verify polynomiality case by case.
